description: This bar chart, from the paper "Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models," displays the percentage point difference in morphosyntactic probing performance across different model layers for two models: the top chart for a baseline model (labeled "concat" on the x-axis) and the bottom chart for the XLM-R model. The horizontal axis in both charts represents the model layer, ranging from 0 to 12, with "concat" indicating the final concatenated layer. The vertical axis, labeled "% point difference," measures the performance difference in percentage points, scaled linearly from -10 to 0, with tick marks at intervals of 2. In the top chart, the bars are colored light blue and show a consistent downward trend, with the bar for layer 0 being the longest (approximately -10.0 percentage points) and the bar for layer 12 being the shortest (approximately -1.0 percentage point). In the bottom chart, the bars are colored dark blue and also show a consistent downward trend, with the bar for layer 0 being the longest (approximately -10.0 percentage points) and the bar for layer 12 being the shortest (approximately -1.0 percentage point). The bars are not sorted and are presented in order of layer index. There is no visual emphasis on any specific bar, and the chart does not include a legend.
